ben_p: Quick dump from this morning's bench: I prototyped a deferred-speculative flow (fast greedy -> async sampler) and wanted to capture oddities.
zara.m: Love the name. Deferred means fallback runs async and may overwrite later, right?
ben_p: Exactly. Fastpath (6B fp16) emits tokens immediately. We spawn an async quantized 70B sampler for tokens where the confidence detector flags low cert. If sampler finishes before client reads we patch; if not, we keep fastpath output.
kai: What detector? entropy / margin?
ben_p: Two-stage detector: 1) token-level margin (top1 - top2) threshold, 2) a tiny L2 "surge" detector over rolling surprisal (window=8) to catch emergent uncertainty. We also track decoder time-to-compute; if sampler latency > budget we stop spawning to avoid wasted compute.
mina_l: Bench numbers? p50/p95/etc.
ben_p: On p50: fastpath-only 72ms, deferred-speculative median stays ~80ms because of spawn overhead, but user-observed perceived latency (what client sees) unchanged when patching happens. p95 improves from 450ms -> 320ms for read-after-patch flows. Overall token-cost ~ -28% vs baseline single 70B.
remy: Interesting. How often does async sampler actually patch?
ben_p: In our 10k mixed benchmark, patch-rate ~9%. Patch tends to be higher on multi-step reasoning and code snippets.
zara.m: Any quality metrics? do async patches improve EM/F1?
ben_p: We measured on our onboarding suites. For factual QA EM: baseline 68.1, fastpath-only 63.9, deferred+patch net 66.9. So patch recovers ~60% of loss. For code-smoke, patch recovered nearly all regressions for short functions but missed some long-context cases.
kai: How do you merge when patch arrives mid-stream? do you reroll following tokens?
ben_p: We have two merge modes: conservative (replace patched tokens and keep the rest) and reroll (force fastpath to re-decode suffix with patched prefix). Reroll cost is higher; we only use it if the merge-signal (KL over next-8 tokens) > threshold. We log both decisions.
mina_l: Any quantization sensitivity? AWQ vs GPTQ?
ben_p: Ran AWQ-int8 and GPTQ-int4. AWQ-int8 patches matched fp16 answers more often. GPTQ-int4 had a higher false-patch rate (it suggested changes that actually lowered EM). So current preference AWQ-int8 for patch sampler.
zara.m: What about hallucinations? if fastpath halluc's with high confidence, detector might not fire.
ben_p: Yep a top-known hole. We tried a tiny discriminator (200M) to score hallucination risk on candidate spans. Running it inline killed perf; we instead run it asynchronously and if it flags we schedule a forced rescore + reroll for that session. Works but complexity increases.
remy: Any production ops issues?
ben_p: A few: 1) resource churn: spawning async jobs causes bursty GPU allocation when many sessions patch simultaneously. 2) session thrash: rapid alternation where patch then reroll then another patch. We added a per-session cooldown (default 3s) and saw thrash drop ~80%. 3) logs balloon: we store both pre/post outputs and diff vectors; storage ops increased.
kai: For resource churn can we use a pooled job queue with backpressure?
ben_p: We're prototyping a priority queue where cheap fastpath jobs have preemptible slots and async patches use lower priority. Also exploring sampling-only lanes on smaller GPUs.
zara.m: Next experiments?
ben_p: Action list: (1) 50k mixed-domain sweep with AWQ-int8 sampler (assigned zara.m), (2) verify cooldown tuning at session-level (assigned kai), (3) cost modeling for Dedicated SKU impact (assigned mina_l), (4) implement low-priority job queue prototype (assigned remy). I'll push experiment configs & logs to s3://redwood-experiments/deferred-spec/3625001234/ and link dashboards.
